tour.welcome.title: Welcome to the tour
tour.welcome.text: In ten stops, this tour shows what sets this application apart from an ordinary editor. Each stop points at the place it is about. You can close the tour at any time and start it again later from the Help menu.
tour.views.title: One document, several views
tour.views.text: The same document in different views: rendered, split, source, live while you write, and as a mind map. This is where you switch; the text itself stays the same.
tour.tabs.title: Several documents side by side
tour.tabs.text: Documents sit in tabs, optionally in two columns side by side. Tabs that belong together can be bundled into a named group with its own color, collapsed and moved as a whole.
tour.sidebars.title: Sidebars and panels
tour.sidebars.text: Left and right are the sidebars with their panels: outline, backlinks, tags, search results, bookmarks and more. Every panel can go to either side, the order is yours, and a finished arrangement can be kept as a named variant.
tour.windows.title: Windows and applications
tour.windows.text: Tabs can be moved out into a further window, for instance onto a second monitor. Beyond that, every additional program start creates a separate application with windows of its own. The window title names application and window.
tour.areas.title: Areas as a working space
tour.areas.text: An area binds an application to a folder including its subfolders. Opening, saving and the recent list then stay inside that boundary. Links to targets outside are marked instead of opened.
tour.subpages.title: Subpages without folder depth
tour.subpages.text: Every page can carry subpages at any depth, independent of the folder structure. The file name is what holds the hierarchy. A breadcrumb above the document shows the parent chain, a panel the direct subpages.
tour.queries.title: Tasks and queries
tour.queries.text: Tasks are ordinary Markdown lines in the text and can still be evaluated. A query inside the document collects tasks, files and properties from the whole search scope and keeps its result current. From the matches you can write back into the source file.
tour.companions.title: The companion files
tour.companions.text: Next to your documents, files appear that you did not create yourself. A document has a companion file with the extension .mdd; it carries history, note and block properties. In an area, the .mdda files for area settings and index are added. They do not appear in the interface, do not open as a document, and travel with the document.
tour.nextSteps.title: Where to go from here
tour.nextSteps.text: The manual answers specific questions; F1 or this menu opens it. To try things out on ready-made material, the File menu creates the bundled Demo-Area as a collection of examples. The tour itself starts from here from now on.
